mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 5.0% over the prior 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 5.0% and the signal is triggered, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is less than 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in the prior month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400.0 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 690000.0 million dollars in the prior month indicates weakening consumer demand, triggering negative equity market returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST < 1400.0 and RSAFS < 690000.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is less than 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by INDPRO growth above 1.0% monthly, capacity constraints trigger inflationary pressures that cause equity market corrections, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO growth exceeds 1.0% monthly, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 690000.0 million dollars in the prior month signals strong consumer spending, supporting earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances where RSAFS exceeds 690000.0 million dollars, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is less than 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 4.5% in the prior month, it indicates aggressive monetary easing that stimulates economic activity and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is less than 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% monthly) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE > 3.5%) signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer income and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both PAYEMS growth is below 0.5% and UNRATE exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is less than 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle regime (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising), policy shifts to combat inflation reduce liquidity and increase discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.01.
